title: Read the bar, or read the number?
hook: Two schools' pass rates on one bar chart. What does the taller bar really tell you?

doesNotKnow: that a bar's length shows the value only when the axis starts at zero

misconception: If one bar is three times as tall as another, its value is about three times as big.
objective: The learner can explain that on a bar chart whose axis does not start at zero, bar heights show only the part above the start, so their ratio exaggerates the ratio of the values.

claims.text: With the axis from 50, bars of 52 and 56 show only the part above 50, heights 2 and 6, so B's bar is 3.00 times as tall (1.33 from 40, 1.08 from 0).
claims.source: Arithmetic: (56 - start)/(52 - start): start 0 -> 1.08, 40 -> 16/12 = 1.33, 50 -> 6/2 = 3.00. Brief 60 check (company/domains/briefs/checks/probability-round4-check.mjs); Demo.tsx ratio().
claims.note: Derivation re-run: (56 - s)/(52 - s) is 1.0769, 1.3333 and 3.0000 for s = 0, 40 and 50; the bars are drawn as value minus start (yOf).

claims.text: B's pass rate is only 1.08 times A's: 56 against 52.
claims.note: Derivation: 56/52 = 1.0769, shown as 1.08. Recall check: 95/91 = 1.044 ('about 4%'), and the bars from 90 are 5 against 1.

claims.text: A bar's length stands for its value only when the bar starts at zero: ratios of bar lengths equal ratios of values only from a zero baseline. On a cut axis, read the numbers, not the heights.
claims.source: Geometry of the chart: length = value - start, so length_B / length_A = value_B / value_A for all values only when start = 0 (brief 60 planned claim 3). Content boundary kept: the claim is about bar lengths, not every chart.
claims.note: Derivation: (b - s)/(a - s) = b/a for all a and b only when s = 0. The claim stays within the brief's limit (bar lengths only).

claims.text: The schools and pass rates are invented.
claims.source: Lesson rule (brief 60 planned claim 4); stage caption 'Pass rates at two invented schools.'
claims.note: Convention, consistent: the caption 'Pass rates at two invented schools.' is on the stage.

recall.question: A bar chart's axis starts at 90. One bar reaches 95, the other 91. One bar looks five times as tall. How do the values compare?
options: One is about five times the other
You can't tell from the chart
recall.why: From a cut axis the bars show only the part above 90 (5 against 1). The values are 95 and 91, about 4% apart: read the numbers, not the heights.
